symptoms: Leaves appear green and healthy
No visible lesions or abnormal discoloration
Normal leaf growth
diseases.prevention: Maintain proper irrigation, nutrition, sanitation and regular monitoring.

symptoms: Yellow or orange spots on leaves
Rust-colored lesions may develop
Premature leaf damage may occur
diseases.treatment: Remove severely affected plant material and use an appropriate fungicide according to local agricultural recommendations and product instructions.
diseases.prevention: Maintain orchard sanitation, remove infected plant debris and monitor plants regularly.

symptoms: Olive-green to dark lesions on leaves
Lesions may become darker as they develop
Affected leaves may become distorted or fall prematurely
diseases.treatment: Remove infected debris and use an appropriate fungicide according to local agricultural recommendations.
diseases.prevention: Maintain orchard sanitation, remove fallen infected leaves and improve air circulation.

symptoms: Gray or tan rectangular lesions on leaves
Lesions may enlarge along leaf veins
Severe infection can reduce healthy leaf area
diseases.treatment: Remove or manage infected crop residues and use recommended fungicide management when appropriate.
diseases.prevention: Use resistant varieties where available, maintain crop rotation and manage crop residues.

symptoms: Elongated brown or tan lesions on leaves
Lesions can expand across the leaf surface
Severe infection may cause premature leaf drying
diseases.treatment: Use appropriate disease-management practices and fungicides where recommended for the crop and region.
diseases.prevention: Use resistant varieties, crop rotation, field sanitation and regular monitoring.

symptoms: Small reddish-brown or rust-colored pustules
Pustules may occur on both sides of leaves
Severe infection can reduce photosynthetic leaf area
diseases.treatment: Use resistant varieties and apply appropriate fungicide management when recommended.
diseases.prevention: Monitor fields regularly, maintain crop health and use resistant varieties where available.

symptoms: Dark brown circular or irregular leaf lesions
Concentric rings may appear inside lesions
Older leaves are commonly affected first
diseases.treatment: Remove heavily infected plant material where practical and use appropriate fungicide management according to local recommendations.
diseases.prevention: Maintain field sanitation, avoid prolonged leaf wetness and practice crop rotation.

symptoms: Leaves appear green and normally developed
No obvious disease lesions
Normal plant growth
diseases.prevention: Maintain balanced nutrition, appropriate irrigation, sanitation and regular crop monitoring.

symptoms: Dark water-soaked lesions on leaves
Brown to black areas may expand rapidly
White fungal growth may appear under humid conditions
diseases.treatment: Remove severely infected material where practical and use appropriate late-blight management products according to local agricultural recommendations.
diseases.prevention: Use healthy planting material, maintain good field sanitation and monitor weather and crop conditions.

symptoms: Leaf discoloration and necrotic areas
Brown or dark lesions may develop
Severe infection can reduce healthy foliage
diseases.treatment: Use appropriate disease-management practices and fungicide treatment when recommended for the identified disease.
diseases.prevention: Maintain field sanitation, crop rotation and regular monitoring.

symptoms: Leaves may curl upward along their margins
Affected leaves may become firm or leathery
Plant growth may be reduced
diseases.treatment: There is no direct cure for a virus-infected plant. Remove severely infected plants where appropriate and manage disease vectors according to local recommendations.
diseases.prevention: Use certified disease-free seed potatoes and control aphid vectors through recommended integrated pest-management practices.

symptoms: Small dark spots on leaves
Spots may develop yellow halos
Fruit may develop small raised or dark lesions
diseases.treatment: Remove severely affected plant material where practical and follow locally recommended bacterial disease-management practices.
diseases.prevention: Use clean planting material, avoid unnecessary leaf wetness and maintain field sanitation.

symptoms: Brown circular lesions on leaves
Concentric ring patterns may develop
Older leaves are often affected first
diseases.treatment: Remove affected plant debris and use an appropriate fungicide according to local recommendations and product instructions.
diseases.prevention: Maintain good field sanitation, crop rotation and avoid prolonged leaf wetness.

symptoms: Leaves are generally green and healthy
No significant disease lesions are visible
Normal plant development
diseases.prevention: Maintain proper irrigation, nutrition, sanitation and regular crop monitoring.

symptoms: Large dark or water-soaked leaf lesions
Lesions can expand quickly
Severe infection can cause rapid leaf deterioration
diseases.treatment: Remove severely infected material where practical and use locally recommended late-blight management practices.
diseases.prevention: Use healthy planting material, maintain sanitation and monitor crop conditions regularly.

symptoms: Yellowish patches may appear on upper leaf surfaces
Olive-green to brown fungal growth may appear on lower leaf surfaces
Leaves may eventually dry and fall
diseases.treatment: Remove affected leaves where practical and improve growing conditions; use an appropriate fungicide when locally recommended.
diseases.prevention: Improve air circulation, reduce excessive humidity and avoid prolonged leaf wetness.

symptoms: Small circular spots with gray centers
Dark margins may surround lesions
Numerous spots can cause premature leaf drop
diseases.treatment: Remove infected leaves and plant debris where practical and use appropriate fungicide management according to local recommendations.
diseases.prevention: Maintain field sanitation, avoid overhead watering and reduce prolonged leaf wetness.
